How to run OpenCode Serve on localhost

For OpenCode 2, bind opencode serve to 127.0.0.1 and set OPENCODE_PASSWORD. Check /api/info with curl. The local server should return 401 without credentials and 200 with the username opencode and your password.

  1. Start a local foreground server
  2. Verify the password and listening address
  3. Connection refused or wrong port
  4. 401 with the correct password
  5. Unexpected 200 or unsure
  6. Test setup and sources

Start a local foreground server

Use a scratch project in a Bash or Zsh terminal. Run opencode --version first. These commands start a separate foreground server on port 4096. Choose another unused port if 4096 is occupied.

IFS= read -rs OPENCODE_PASSWORD
OPENCODE_PASSWORD="$OPENCODE_PASSWORD" opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096

After entering the first command, type a fresh password and press Enter. The terminal hides your input. Keep that terminal open and keep its startup output private, since it can display the password. Press Ctrl+C to stop the server, then run unset OPENCODE_PASSWORD in that shell.

For same-machine access, use the loopback bind even when you set a password. The API controls a process that can access project files and run tools as its host user. Plain HTTP Basic auth provides no transport encryption.

Verify the password and listening address

Open a second terminal. The second curl command prompts for your password so it stays out of the command line.

curl --noproxy '*' -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4096/api/info
curl --noproxy '*' -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -u opencode http://127.0.0.1:4096/api/info

Expect 401 and 200, in that order. On macOS, run lsof -nP -iTCP:4096 -sTCP:LISTEN. Check that the OpenCode listener reads 127.0.0.1:4096. A successful HTTP check alone says nothing about the other addresses the process listens on.

What did curl return?

Check the portCheck credentialsVerify the listener

Connection refused or wrong port

Check the terminal where you started opencode serve and confirm it is still running. If the port is taken, choose another unused port when restarting and change the port in both curl commands. In OpenCode 2, the shared background service is a separate process. Use opencode service status if that was the instance you meant to inspect.

401 with the correct password

Confirm the URL points to your foreground server, the Basic username is exactly opencode, and the password was available when that process started. If you changed it afterward, stop and restart that foreground process and repeat both checks.

In V2, prefer OPENCODE_PASSWORD. The older OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD also worked in 2.4.1. V2 uses the fixed username opencode. For V1, use its own server API and authentication settings. OpenCode authentication migration guide

Unexpected 200 or unsure

If /api/info returns 200 without credentials or the listener reports a wildcard address, stop the foreground process you started. Confirm the process and port with lsof, then restart explicitly on 127.0.0.1 with a password. Test that unauthenticated and authenticated requests now give 401 and 200 before using it in a real project.

For a port you cannot identify, run the tests against a fresh foreground server on an unused port. If you ran curl against /, repeat the check against /api/info.

Test setup and sources

Tested OpenCode 2.4.1 on Apple Silicon macOS on November 28, 2026, using two temporary profiles with networking restricted to loopback. Each foreground process listened on 127.0.0.1. With either password variable, no credentials, a wrong username and a wrong password each returned 401. The configured password with username opencode returned 200.
